title: Morningside Financial - Dedicated capacity discovery
topics: dedicated GPU sizing and burst strategy
summary: Initial discovery for Dedicated capacity. Customer currently on a mix of hosted APIs and on-prem experimentation; primary asks are predictable throughput for real-time products, strict data isolation, and a burst plan for periodic peak traffic. Security team requested SOC2/ISO artifacts and details on KMS/HSM integration. Agreed next step: Redwood to send pricing, SOW options for Dedicated + Private control plane, and benchmark plan for 2-week pilot.

Luis to share benchmark checklist and preferred latency/load tests (by 2026-03-05)

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time (UTC): 14:23
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees:
 - Samira Patel (Redwood, AE)
 - Luis Ortega (Redwood, SE)
 - Rebecca Lin (Morningside, Head of AI)
 - Daniel Park (Morningside, Infra Lead)
 - Karen Soto (Morningside, Security)
 - Omar Aziz (Morningside, Product)

Auto-summary (auto): Customer evaluating dedicated/reserved GPU capacity for low-latency production features; security/compliance and burst scaling are top concerns.

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, um we're excited to dive in. Quick intro around table - Luis I'll let you do a quick technical pitch and then we'll go into questions.
[00:15] Luis: Yeah thanks Samira. Hi Rebecca, Daniel, Karen - I'll keep it short, we're hoping to understand your workload shapes, SLOs, and constraints so we can propose a Dedicated configuration. Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, private VPC option, and burst capacity - sorry I said re-dwood there - um variants and fallbacks too.
[00:34] Rebecca: Great. For context, we've been prototyping with a mix of hosted APIs - some OpenAI, some internal smaller models running on prem. Our main user-facing product is a financial assistant that needs sub-150ms p99 in inference for short prompts, and we have nightly batch jobs for embeddings. We're trying to figure out whether Dedicated vs Hosted fits our latency and isolation requirements.
[00:56] Daniel: Also from infra side, we need guaranteed throughput during market opens - spikes up to 6x baseline for 15-30 minutes. We want reserved capacity so the app doesn't degrade. Burst handling is huge.
[01:12] Samira: Understood. Can you share your baseline qps and the 6x peak numbers? Even ballpark helps.
[01:20] Rebecca: Right now baseline is around 60 QPS for generation endpoints, peaks to about 360 during open. Latency target: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 ideally < 150ms.
[01:35] Luis: Okay that's helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs - what's your typical seq length and model family? Short prompts or long docs?
[01:44] Rebecca: Mostly short prompts, 64 tokens typical. But there are also customer support queries that hit ~512 tokens occasionally. We use a mix: a tuned open Llama variant internally and sometimes Anthropic for sensitive content.
[02:01] Karen: From security, we need data isolation - we can't have any customer data landing on shared tenants. SOC2 is required, plus encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS for the Dedicated. Is HSM support available?
[02:19] Luis: Yes - Redwood Dedicated supports a private control plane and VPC deployments. We integrate with customer KMS and offer HSM-backed key management in certain plans. I'll share the compliance pack after this call.
[02:33] Daniel: How does autoscaling and burst work? We want reserved baseline but also able to spin up additional GPUs for a short window - without breaking isolation or adding huge cold start latency.
[02:46] Samira: Good question. The typical pattern is reserved GPU pool for your baseline, and a burst pool that's either shared across tenants or dedicated depending on contract. For strict isolation you can get dedicated burst capacity - that would be part of the Dedicated contract. There's also fast warm-up via pre-warmed containers and KV cache priming to reduce cold-start token costs.
[03:08] Rebecca: Are there fallback policies? If our primary model is busy, can we fall back to a smaller quantized variant to keep latency under SLO?
[03:17] Luis: Yep, smart routing supports fallbacks. You can pin rollouts and route by latency or cost policy. If you want absolute predictability, you can pin capacity to the exact model variant across the pool.
[03:28] Omar: On the cost side, we need unit economics. How much of the cost is per-token vs reserved node cost? And do you have tooling to show token-level costs?
[03:40] Samira: On Dedicated, it's primarily reserved capacity pricing (monthly commit) plus usage for burst. Our Console shows token-level breakdowns and per-route cost, and Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching settings to save dollars while meeting latency.
[03:58] Karen: Another security Q - audit logging and traceability. We need full request logs for audit, ideally stored in our S3 and with fine-grained RBAC. Can we route logs to our SIEM?
[04:12] Luis: Yes. Dedicated + Private control plane can push audit logs to your storage/SIEM and we support SAML SSO, RBAC, and per-token tracing hooks. We'll include sample log schema in the compliance pack.
[04:27] Daniel: Ok technical dive - what GPU types do you recommend for our workload? 64-token mostly, p99 <150ms.
[04:36] Luis: For short prompts, A100 class or H100 give best p99. For production cost balance, we often suggest V100/A10 or 80GB A10x depending on model size. If you're serving 13B-ish Llama family models, 80GB Vram with certain kernel optimizations works well. We can run benchmarks to pick the right size.
[04:55] Rebecca: We also care about quantization - can you serve 4-bit quantized models on Dedicated and do you see latency regressions?
[05:04] Luis: Yes, quantization is supported; latency usually improves but it depends on kernel and sequence length. We'll test your model with our compilation paths - sometimes small accuracy tradeoffs happen, we pair that with eval sets.
[05:20] [short cross-talk] Daniel: (inaudible) - so benchmarks are important.
[05:25] Luis: Absolutely. We propose a benchmark plan: you provide representative request traces and we'll run a mix of p99 latency and throughput tests across candidate GPU configs. We typically do a 72-hour soak with spike windows to validate autoscaling and burst.
[05:42] Rebecca: That sounds fair. Timeline? We're hoping to have a pilot in April.
[05:47] Samira: If we get the data and sign the pilot SOW by mid-March, we can have infra ready in early April. Pilot typically runs 2 weeks.
[05:58] Karen: One more security detail - where do model weights live in Private deployments? We need to ensure weights are customer-controlled and not copied to third-party blob storage.
[06:10] Luis: In a Private control plane deployment, weights are stored on customer-managed storage. For Hosted Dedicated we provide encryption in transit and at rest, and KMS integration; weights are in the customer's tenancy if you opt for Private. We'll detail this in the SOW.
[06:26] Omar: For burst pricing, do you do overage per GPU-hour or per-token?
[06:32] Samira: Burst is typically billed as incremental GPU-hour blocks or vCPU/GPU-second; tokens only matter on hosted usage. We'll include estimated cost models in the pricing sheet.
[06:44] Rebecca: Are there any known limits around concurrent KV cache sizes and multi-tenant memory thrash? We rely on prefix caching for repeated queries.
[06:54] Luis: Early memory management is per-process; we have continuous batching and KV cache management to avoid thrash. For Dedicated you'll get isolated cache allocations. There's also pre-warm priming to ensure warm KV hits.
[07:10] [15 minutes later - timestamp jump] [15:05] Daniel: Quick question on integrations - we want integration with our internal observability, can we get trace ids correlated with APM?
[15:15] Luis: Yes, we surface trace ids and can push to your Jaeger/Zipkin or Datadog.
[15:22] Karen: On compliance pack - will you provide SOC2 Type II report and pen test briefs?
[15:28] Samira: We will share SOC2 reports and a redacted pen test summary. For the deeper pen test, we can coordinate under NDA.
[15:36] Rebecca: For the pilot, can we request a dedicated GPU pool sized to handle 2x peak so we can test fallbacks?
[15:44] Luis: Yes we can size the pilot for that. Note that dedicated 2x peak will affect monthly commit - we'll model costs.
[15:52] Omar: For routing, do you support canary rollouts between model versions without downtime?
[15:58] Luis: Absolutely - rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies are built in.
[16:05] [late in call - negotiation tone] Rebecca: If we sign a 12-month commit, are there discounts on reserved capacity and on HSM add-ons?
[16:14] Samira: Yes, multi-year or 12-month commits get progressive discounts and we can include HSM as an add-on with preferred pricing. I'll send an example tiered pricing table.
[16:24] Karen: Please clarify data residency - we need EU-hosted logs for EU customers. Does Dedicated let us pick regions?
[16:32] Luis: Yes, we support region pinning for Dedicated pools and logs can be routed to regionally controlled S3 buckets.
[16:40] [closing] Samira: Ok last bit - next steps recap: we'll send pricing/SOW, Luis sends benchmark checklist, customer shares traffic traces and compliance asks, and we'll schedule a follow-up technical demo next week. Anything else?
[16:58] Rebecca: No, that covers it. Thanks.
[17:02] Samira: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up by Friday with the docs.
[17:06] End of recording.
